n: Someone who stays stubborn after repeated correction will suddenly be broken beyond repair.

f.g: Becomes stiff-necked—like an ox refusing the yoke.

n: When the righteous lead, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan. The Book of Mormon’s King Mosiah taught this same truth about government.

f.w: When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice

n: A child who loves wisdom makes the father glad; one who keeps company with prostitutes wastes his wealth—like the prodigal son.
A king who rules with justice stabilizes a land; one who demands bribes or heavy taxes tears it down.

f.g: One who takes bribes, or a man of heavy levies.

n: Flattering a neighbor is like spreading a net for his feet—it sets him up to fall.
Evildoers are trapped by their own sin, but the righteous sing and rejoice.
The righteous care about justice for the poor; the wicked don’t even want to know.

f.w: considereth the cause of the poor

n: Mockers stir up a whole city, but the wise calm the anger.

f.w: bring a city into a snare
f.g: Set a city aflame with unrest.

n: When a wise person takes a fool to court, the fool only rages or laughs, and there’s no peace. Some disputes can’t be won.
The bloodthirsty hate people of integrity, but the upright care for their lives.
A fool vents all his anger, but a wise person quietly holds it back.

f.w: A fool uttereth all his mind
f.g: mind = spirit, temper—he lets it all out.

n: If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials will become corrupt. Leaders set the tone for those under them.
The poor and their oppressor have this in common: the Lord gives light to the eyes of both. God gives life to all.

f.w: the LORD lighteneth both their eyes

n: A king who judges the poor fairly will have a throne established forever.

f.w: his throne shall be established for ever

n: Discipline and correction impart wisdom; a child left without guidance brings shame to his mother.
When the wicked increase, so does sin—but the righteous will see their downfall.

f.w: the righteous shall see their fall

n: Discipline your child, and he will give you peace and delight.
Where there is no revelation from God, people run wild; blessed is the one who keeps God’s law. “Vision” here means prophetic revelation, not just planning.

f.w: Where there is no vision, the people perish
f.g: vision = prophetic revelation; perish = cast off restraint, run wild.

f.w: he that keepeth the law, happy is he

n: A servant can’t be corrected by words alone; even if he understands, he won’t respond.
There’s more hope for a fool than for someone who speaks rashly.
A servant pampered from childhood may in the end become insolent or claim to be family. The Hebrew of the last word is uncertain.

f.g: The Hebrew word is rare; it may mean “heir” or “trouble.”

n: An angry person stirs up conflict, and a hot-tempered one commits many sins.

f.w: An angry man stirreth up strife

n: Pride brings a person low, but the humble in spirit gain honor.

f.w: A man's pride shall bring him low

n: An accomplice to a thief harms himself: he hears the oath to testify but stays silent. Covering for wrongdoing makes you guilty too.

f.g: He hears the curse placed on anyone who withholds testimony.

n: Fear of what people think is a trap, but trusting the Lord keeps you safe.

f.w: The fear of man bringeth a snare

n: Many seek favor from rulers, but true justice comes from the Lord.

f.w: every man's judgment cometh from the LORD

n: The righteous detest the dishonest, and the wicked detest the upright. The Hezekiah collection ends with the two ways in clear contrast.
